renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: gsea_dotplot
  title: Enriched gene sets
  description: |-
    Each dot is a gene set: its normalised enrichment score (NES) on the horizontal axis, its size by the number of genes in the set and its colour by the FDR q-value. It answers which pathways move together at one end of the ranked gene list, and in which direction.
    How to read: a set far from zero with a dark colour is strongly and confidently enriched. A positive NES means enrichment at the top of the ranked list and a negative one at the bottom, so compare both poles before concluding. Sets with few genes can reach a high score by chance, so look at the size too.
    Lines and annotations: this plot keeps only sets with an FDR q-value up to 0.25, the cut-off at which the GSEA report highlights sets as most likely to give interesting hypotheses. The report itself still gives results for every set, and the table below lists them all. The user guide advises a stricter 5% when the run has few samples and permutes gene sets rather than phenotypes.
    Source: https://docs.gsea-msigdb.org/#GSEA/GSEA_User_Guide/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16199517/
  kind: enrichment
  config:
    padj_threshold: 0.25
    top_n: 20
    default_colour_by: neg_log10_padj
  roles:
    term: term
    nes: nes
    padj: fdr_qvalue
    gene_count: size
    source: phenotype

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gsea_nes_bars
  title: Top gene sets by enrichment score
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene set: its normalised enrichment score in a contrast, for the sets with the largest absolute score. It answers which pathways drive each contrast and at which pole.
    How to read: long bars to the right are enriched in the positive pole and to the left in the negative one. A bar that is marked passes the FDR cut-off, while an unmarked long bar is a strong score that is not significant, so check the dot plot and the table.
    Lines and annotations: bars are marked when the FDR q-value is below 0.25, the cut-off the GSEA report highlights.
    Source: https://docs.gsea-msigdb.org/#GSEA/GSEA_User_Guide/
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.25
    effect_label: Normalised enrichment score (NES)
  roles:
    feature_id: term
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: nes
    significance: fdr_qvalue
    label: phenotype

- component: card
  title: Gene sets reported
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene sets in the report tables, with the row count next to it, and the bars split them by the pole they came up at. It answers how many sets each end of the ranking holds.
    How to read: a very uneven split means the contrast mostly pushes expression one way. A set listed under both poles of different contrasts appears in each.
  column: term
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: phenotype
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: gene sets, by pole

- component: card
  title: Strongest enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest absolute normalised enrichment score of any set, with the spread of the absolute scores in the box. It answers how strong the top signal is.
    How to read: the sign is dropped because the strongest set can sit at either pole. A box close to the maximum means many sets are strongly enriched, and a low box with a few outliers means a few standout sets.
  column: abs_nes
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: strongest set, with the spread

- component: card
  title: FDR q-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median FDR q-value over the reported sets, with the lowest and the highest next to it and the bar placed against the two cut-offs. It answers how confident the enrichment calls are overall.
    How to read: a median in the green band is a strongly supported result. A median between the two cut-offs is acceptable for exploration, and above them the reported sets are mostly noise.
    Lines and annotations: 0.25 is the cut-off the GSEA report highlights and 0.05 the stricter one the user guide advises for few samples with gene-set permutation.
    Source: https://docs.gsea-msigdb.org/#GSEA/GSEA_User_Guide/
  column: fdr_qvalue
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  threshold_warn: 0.25
  caption: median q-value, with the best and the worst

- component: card
  title: Leading-edge share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a set's genes that form its leading edge, the genes that drive the enrichment score, with the spread in the box. It answers whether enrichment comes from a few genes or from most of the set.
    How to read: a high share means most of the set moves together, and a low share that a few genes carry the score. Read the leading-edge genes of a set in the table before interpreting it.
  column: leading_edge_percent
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: table
  title: Enrichment report
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene set in one contrast and pole: its size, scores, p-values, FDR q-value and leading edge. It answers which sets to follow up and which genes drive them.
    How to read: sort by FDR q-value, keep the sets below the cut-off and read their leading-edge genes. Click a row to filter the other tiles to that set.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: term
